book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Male representative with fibre

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A man who sits in Parliament is credited with strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with fibre' reads as moral fibre; it is a plant fibre instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is a plant whose tough stem strands are spun into rope and cloth, so it is a natural fibre.

clue.text: The sculpture is not right in height

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter standing for right is taken away

parts.note: stature is a person's height
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A critic complains a sculpted figure is out of proportion in its height.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, a three-dimensional work of art of the kind called a sculpture.

clue.text: Mother at home serving master — that's normal!

indicators.note: serving dishes up a word in a new form, as food is arranged on a plate, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
someone at home is in
the six letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother staying home to wait on the head of the house is presented as the ordinary state of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving master' reads as domestic service; 'serving' is a loose anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainstream is the prevailing, conventional current of opinion or taste, so as an adjective it means ordinary.

clue.text: Father called for a knife

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
to have rung someone on the phone is to have called them

explanation.surface: A father phoned to ask for a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: A parang is a heavy Malay chopping knife, like a machete; the solver has to see the two short words run together into one unfamiliar one.
explanation.definitionFit: A parang is a large broad-bladed blade used in Malaysia and Indonesia for cutting vegetation, a type of knife.

clue.text: Baton Rouge initially welcomed the French martinet

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the French article goes inside
initially points to the first letter of the word it follows, which is added at the end

parts.note: a baton is a stick
le is French for the
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A strict officer is welcomed to Baton Rouge, the Louisiana city.
explanation.walkthrough: Baton Rouge looks like one place name, the capital of Louisiana, but the two words do separate jobs: one is a synonym, the other supplies only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, and a stickler is someone who insists on every rule being followed exactly.

clue.text: Something of jazz included in metal?

indicators.note: something of a word is just a part of it, here a single letter taken from it

parts.note: one letter of the word, its final one
inc. is the abbreviation for included or inclusive

explanation.surface: It wonders whether a bit of jazz has found its way into heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal' suggests heavy metal rock alongside jazz; it is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white element used in galvanising and brass, so it is a metal.

clue.text: One provides for the Italian coming back during meal

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the Italian article is read from right to left

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone caters for an Italian guest returning in the middle of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier is a person or firm that furnishes goods, literally one who provides them.

clue.text: Agreed resolution by small community

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an arrangement ending a dispute
second meaning: a place where people have set up home, a village or colony

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a village vote; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a deal that resolves a disagreement and a small place where people have established homes.

clue.text: Bonus ball?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something additional, more than was due
second meaning: in cricket a no-ball or wide adds a run to the batting side's score under this heading

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a lottery term, the bonus ball drawn after the main numbers. In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery, and the run it gives away is counted as one of these; the question mark flags that ball is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an addition beyond the norm, and in cricket scoring it is the category for runs from no-balls and wides.

clue.text: Characteristic of homage paid after a time

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
a tribute is homage paid to someone

explanation.surface: A writer describes a feature of the respect shown to someone long after their day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid after' suggests the order of the pieces: the homage comes after 'a time'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a quality or feature belonging to someone, the same as a characteristic.

clue.text: Flower power? Auntie got worried

indicators.note: someone worried is agitated and unsettled, so the letters of the aunt are stirred out of order

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
the six letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A 1960s hippy slogan alarms an elderly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower power' looks like one hippy phrase; it splits into the definition and a single letter. Auntie is also a nickname for the BBC, another false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a garden plant grown for its trumpet-shaped blooms, so it is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Where a pilot might trigger mine?

parts.note: to cock a gun is to set its trigger mechanism ready to fire
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: It asks where an aviator could set off an explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the wordplay: where a pilot might cock (trigger) something. 'trigger' and 'mine' look like a weapon and its explosive, but they are verb and noun pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment at the front of an aircraft where the flier sits at the controls is the cockpit.

clue.text: Start of summer thaw means fish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the season's name
to thaw is to melt

explanation.surface: As summer arrives and the ice thaws, the fish start running.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelt is a small silvery food fish of northern waters, so it is one kind of fish.

clue.text: Altercation over measures for disposal here

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel
yards are units of length

explanation.surface: A dispute about quantities of waste for dumping breaks out at a site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is placement only: the quarrel sits over, above, the measures in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard is where old cars and metal are taken to be broken up, a place of disposal.

clue.text: As leaving, break cover with 6

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so the letters of these words are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: Like a hunted animal leaving its hiding place, something breaks cover, though the 6 reference sits oddly in the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break cover' looks like a single phrase about game bolting from shelter, but 'break' works alone on the words before it. 6 is the answer to 6 Down, ZINC.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise iron or steel is to coat it with zinc to stop rust, so it means covering with that metal.

clue.text: Perhaps too involved in punctuation?

indicators.note: involved means tangled or convoluted, so the letters of the two words are mixed up together

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: It wonders if a little word such as 'too' plays a part in punctuating text.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'punctuation', yet the whole clue also hints that a mark might be involved in how a word like too is written.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a mark showing omission or possession, one item of punctuation; the noun covers the marks collectively.

clue.text: A study of sorbet?

parts.note: surface reading: an academic investigation of a frozen dessert
setter's reading: a sorbet served between dinner stages livens the palate, and a short study course that brings knowledge up to date has the same name

explanation.walkthrough: A sorbet is traditionally served between courses of a formal meal to refresh the palate, so it is literally a refresher course; the phrase also means a short training class.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is a brief programme of study updating earlier training, so it fits 'a study', with the dessert pun behind it.

clue.text: Leave coat found on lake

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a coat which is later found by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places one piece after the other in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlough is a leave of absence granted to soldiers or employees, so it is a noun sense of leave.

clue.text: Pest making call at bingo — cunning!

parts.note: a player shouts 'house' on completing a card at bingo
fly is British slang for sharp or cunning

explanation.surface: A tiresome person in a bingo hall makes a sly call.
explanation.definitionFit: The housefly is a common insect that spreads disease, a typical domestic pest.

clue.text: Golf score — total is crucial

parts.note: par is the standard score for a hole of golf
an amount is a total, a sum

explanation.surface: On the golf course, the final tally decides everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means of supreme importance, above all else, which is close to the sense of vital or crucial.

clue.text: Watches male involved in rows

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a man who is caught up in quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests quarrels, rhyming with cows; here it means lines of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Timers are devices that measure elapsed time, as watches do, so the plural nouns correspond.

clue.text: What a doctor should do with delicacy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: give medical care to a patient
second meaning: a special tasty item of food or a pleasure

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a doctor's tact or bedside manner, delicacy as gentleness; it is in fact a sweet or titbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's job is to give medical attention, and a nice morsel is also called by this same word as a noun.

clue.text: Lie about team having right magic mixture

indicators.note: about can mean in a roundabout way, turned around, so the letters of the falsehood are shuffled

parts.note: the three letters of this word rearranged
XI, Roman eleven, is a cricket or football team
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone tells untruths about a team that has the winning formula.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical potion supposed to cure ills or prolong life, so it is an enchanted mixture.

clue.text: To a nice cook, it is poison

indicators.note: to cook figures or accounts is to tamper with them, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters of these three words, taken together

explanation.surface: A warning that some dish, harmless to most, is toxic to a refined chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a plant whose extract is a deadly toxin, so it names a poison.

clue.text: One argument against 2

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: It looks like a single point raised against the answer to 2 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is the answer to 2 Down, STATUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or figure that is venerated, so it can stand in for a statue.

clue.text: Tying up the doctor with call on old

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
O is the abbreviation for old
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone keeps the doctor busy with a visit to an elderly patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call on' looks like the phrase meaning visit, but 'on' only places the call after old.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring is the act of securing a boat in place with ropes, which is tying it up.

clue.text: The attendance is good — a hollow tribute!

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

indicators.note: something hollow has its inside emptied, so only the outer letters of the word survive

parts.note: the word with its middle emptied out, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A good turnout at a memorial event turns out to be an empty gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: The gate is the number of spectators at a sports match, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gate is the word for the crowd paying to watch a sporting event, so it means the attendance.

clue.text: 'It is symbolic of the clergy to follow arrest

definitions.text: It is symbolic of the clergy

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
to collar a suspect is slang for arresting them

explanation.surface: Something representing churchmen is set to come after an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white band worn by priests and ministers is the mark of the clergy, their emblem.

clue.text: The entertainer accepts one for a lift

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a host entertains guests
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer agrees to give somebody a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertainer' suggests a comedian or singer; here it is the one who entertains guests at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for raising heavy things, a kind of lift or crane.
